summary: Best possible lineup of each of 138 past weeks: QB + 1 or more WR/TE teammates in 60% (ordinary lineups 22%); stack (1+) with a bring-back in 14% (ordinary lineups 4%); at most 3 offensive players from one team in 99% (ordinary lineups 100%).

Stacks and teams, 138 weeks before kickoff: qb + 2 + bring-back, nobody facing the defense put 1.36x as many lineups in a week's top 5% as ordinary lineups (95% interval 1.19-1.58; 2.3x in the top 1%); 6 of 9 rule sets cleared 1.0.
3 rule set(s) were indistinguishable from ordinary lineups: at most 3 from one team; qb + 1 pass catcher + a bring-back; qb + 1 + bring-back, at most 3 from a team.
Spending by position, 138 weeks before kickoff: no rule set cleared 1.0 on the top-5% rate by more than week-to-week noise.
15 rule sets were indistinguishable from ordinary lineups.

Game totals and opposing defenses, 138 weeks before kickoff: at most 1 player faces one of the 8 toughest defenses for his position put 1.12x as many lineups in a week's top 5% as ordinary lineups (95% interval 1.01-1.23; 1.4x in the top 1%); 1 of 9 rule sets cleared 1.0.
8 rule sets were indistinguishable from ordinary lineups.

Combinations, 138 weeks before kickoff: qb + 2 + bring-back, 5+ players from implied totals of 24+ put 1.33x as many lineups in a week's top 5% as ordinary lineups (95% interval 1.14-1.56; 2.4x in the top 1%); 3 of 5 rule sets cleared 1.0.
2 rule set(s) were indistinguishable from ordinary lineups: cheaper qb + at most one $8,000+ + one te; qb + 1 + bring-back + the salary shape.

With the FantasyPoints projections (11 weeks of 2026): qb + 2 + bring-back, 5+ players against weak defenses put 1.90x as many lineups in a week's top 5% as ordinary lineups (95% interval 1.13-3.08; 5.3x in the top 1%); 6 of 38 rule sets cleared 1.0.
Rules that hurt: te at $5,500 or more (0.53x).
31 rule sets were indistinguishable from ordinary lineups.
caveats: The best lineups are chosen after the scores are known, so a trait can be common among them only because of which players happened to score. The forward test is the check on that.
Salaries are on file for 2014-2021 and 2026 only (138 main slates). DraftKings pricing and the league's scoring environment have changed since, so older weeks count as evidence, not as a forecast.

The forward test projects players from their salary (what a player at that price has averaged in the other seasons), so every lineup that spends the cap has about the same expected points. It isolates what structure does to the spread of scores. It says nothing about whether your projections beat the salary-implied ones.

A lineup counts as a top-5% (top-1%) lineup when it beats the 95th (99th) percentile of every lineup built that week by every rule set, a stand-in for a field with many kinds of lineups. The lift is a rule set's rate over the unconstrained optimizer's. Measured against the unconstrained lineups alone, nearly every rule looked better (even opposite ones), because those lineups are too alike to serve as a yardstick; against the pooled field, rules that only change which players are used (the spending rules) show no lift.

Forty-odd rule sets were tested, so a couple would clear a 95% interval by chance alone: a single 'better' that is not a stack, and does not repeat on 2026 with the FantasyPoints projections, is not evidence.
Ownership rules are not tested: there is no historical ownership data, so the screen's ownership figures are a heuristic ordering.

The Millionaire Maker pays its top prize to roughly one lineup in a hundred thousand. This study measures landing in the top 5% and 1% of ordinary lineups, the closest proxy a sample this size allows, not contest results.
